semanticText:
# Reservation Clause

Maintains group proposals and reservation decisions on an Order. `snapshot` defaults to `/orderSnapshot`, `state` to `/reservations`, `requests` to `/reservationRequests` and `timing` to `/cancellationTiming`. When a snapshot exists, initialization validates its frozen terms, quote and groups and creates their reservation state. Without a snapshot, there are no initial group reservations. A configured customer role can pin the Order's customer account to the roster.

A group can wait for the supplier or customer, be confirmed or fulfilled, or end by cancellation, decline, expiry or no-show. Automatic confirmation of a group without a schedule can confirm without a service start. For scheduled groups it requires valid supplier readiness, a future start and immediate-charge consent when the agreed terms require it. Configured confirmation, alternative and acceptance actions identify the exact reviewed proposal. Each request key records the action, input and actor. An identical repeat is a duplicate. Key conflicts and stale proposals fail.

When `reviewedSellerActivation` is enabled, seller confirmation or an alternative and customer acceptance require the exact Order version and the expected role. The reviewed scope includes the Order, seller, activation revision, terms, selected Payment Instruction, exact proposal, start, amount and currency. The admitted payment must match the Order and have sufficient confirmed secured funds with no pending secure, capture or void reservation. A seller alternative can record the grant while awaiting customer acceptance. The customer must accept against that same grant. A confirmed reviewed group can record seller approval in Activation.

Cancellation actions require an explicit snapshot cancellation policy and a matching reviewed proposal. A customer's configured elapsed-hour window starts at the first recorded actual Order activation. A configured before-start window must match the agreed service terms and requires a confirmed start. The elapsed condition uses this time when available. An explicitly bound fallback can supply evidence for eligible untimestamped automatic activation. The free cutoffs are inclusive. If both conditions apply, the first cutoff ends the free period. For the elapsed-only undated path, a pending group can cross the elapsed cutoff. Timed service guards still apply when a confirmed service start exists.

A terminal decision records the actor, reason, time, proposal identity, basis, charge and amount designated for release in the frozen quote currency. Supplier cancellation records no late charge. A configured no-show decision applies the agreed charge at or after the confirmed start. Expiry requires a reached response deadline. The decision records payment evidence required. The Payment Instruction records any later capture, void or refund separately.

A service-relative-only condition can use the confirmed service start after any seller-confirmation prerequisite. It has no elapsed clock requirement. The decision can record the available Order activation time in `orderActivatedAtMicros`.

When `rememberCancellationActivation` is connected, it records the first qualifying actual activation as a positive Unix-microsecond timestamp at the `timing` binding plus `/activatedAtMicros`, defaulting to `/cancellationTiming/activatedAtMicros`. An absent timestamp leaves the activation-based elapsed start unverified, including initialization without a positive execution time. If `sellerConfirmationRequired` is true, recording also requires seller approval. With that flag, customer cancellation before seller approval and before the timestamp is recorded is free and records `beforeSellerConfirmation`. After that evidence arrives, cancellation evaluates the configured window and service guards.

When `cancellationRequiresCapture` is true, a positive cancellation charge requires the admitted instruction's cumulative confirmed captures to equal the full Order amount. A capture that has only been requested cannot satisfy this guard. `CANCELLATION_AWAITING_CAPTURE` leaves the decision unapplied so it can be retried after confirmation. Free cancellation can record its decision without this capture check.

When the frozen cancellation policy covers one whole-Order group, the clause also projects the matching group ID, status, proposal amount and any terminal decision reference at `/wholeOrderReservation`. An absent projection gives no evidence of a whole-Order group. The group records remain the source for proposal and decision details.

## Automatic activation without a timestamp

`authorizationTimingFallback` has no default. The only supported configured value is `/payment/authorizationTiming`. When the connected activation action observes an automatically active Order during initialization without a timestamp or processing event, it can record `initializedWithoutTimestamp` below the `timing` binding. A recorded Order activation time always takes precedence.

For an elapsed condition, the fallback requires this marker, automatic confirmation, an empty required-approval roster, active and ready Order access, and matching preparation evidence for the original selected or usable Payment Instruction. The Order and instruction must share a positive full amount and currency. A valid receipt supplies a positive Unix-microsecond `authorizedAtMicros` and the ID of the matching successful full `secure` request. That time can appear on the decision as `paymentAuthorizedAtMicros`, separately from Order activation evidence.

When selection or full authorization is still pending, the elapsed condition waits and the decision can record `paymentAuthorizationPending`. An applicable service-relative condition continues to use the confirmed service start. A successful full authorization with a missing or invalid receipt cannot supply the elapsed start. An absent binding leaves this fallback unavailable.
